output.brief:
The evidence points to the data, not the operators. On 3 Oct, Regulatory Affairs entered a 36-month shelf life for Veltranol with a valid-from date of 1 Mar 2027. The 24-month value is still the one in effect. From 4 Oct, the data PackBridge sent to the printers carried 36 months. That is despite the vendor saying it can't send future values. Every Veltranol job before that matched the batch record, including jobs run by agency operators after the firmware change. Every job after it was 12 months late. No operator overrides were made, and the printed text matched what was sent. The camera only checks print against the job, so it passed everything. Two jobs on Line 1 day shift, run by permanent staff, are affected too. They are in the warehouse. That rules out operators and firmware, and the agency-operator theory with them. Warnings would punish the wrong people. Switching off the camera check would remove a useful control.

Next steps:
- Fix the Veltranol shelf-life records.
- Hold every Veltranol lot packed since 4 Oct, including the two Line 1 lots.
- Add a second-person check of printed expiry against the batch record at each setup.
- Check retained cartons of the two other products with future-dated edits (HX-15-30 and MR-05-14).
- Ask Corvane and IT why PackBridge sent a future-dated value.

I'm not sure whether other products are affected.
